newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Market steady as sellers return.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Market steady as sellers return.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market edged down slightly on Wednesday despite sharply higher swaps values as physical sellers returned to the market to moderate the spiralling swaps prices, traders said.
August fuel oil swaps rose to trade at an intra-day high of $104.25 per tonne before easing slightly late day after physical sellers emerged to last quote at $103.75/$104.25, brokers said.
August was quoted on Tuesday at $102.50/$103.00, they said.
Late Wednesday, two physical sellers offered 20,000-tonne lots each at $104.00 and $105.00 per tonne but there were no buyers against it.
The absence of buyers led some players to speculate that the market might come under fresh physical selling pressure from players who felt that the market has been over-bought.
But others argued that strong bunker demand could underpin the latest rally as the market is still suffering from tight supplies.
Bunker prices have risen by about $3.00 per tonne since Monday and was poised to rise further due to strong demand from shipowners, traders said.
The scarce prompt availabilties have already forced some shipowners to pay a premium of over $5.00 per tonne above current prices to secure bunker for lifting over the next few days.
Traders said the tight supplies in Singapore is expected to persists for the rest of this month because no additional export cargoes are due to arrive from the Middle East.
Also Singapore refiners are processing more condensates and light and middle distillate rich crudes, they said.
Some additional supplies are coming into the market with Sri Lanka issuing a tender to sell 19,000 tonnes of 180-cst, 3.5-pct sulphur fuel oil for August 27-28 lifting, closing 13.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
